title: Advanced Data Sufficiency
tagline: Year 3 — Deciding whether the given statements are enough to answer a question, without solving it fully

introduction.overview: A data-sufficiency question asks a question and gives two statements. You do not have to find the answer; you have to decide whether the statements provide enough information to find it. There are four outcomes: statement I alone is enough, statement II alone is enough, both together are needed, or even both together are not enough. The discipline is to judge each statement separately first, then together, and never to bring in outside facts.
introduction.placementRelevance: Data-sufficiency items appear in logical-reasoning and quantitative sections of company tests, especially in management-oriented hiring.
introduction.realWorldContext: Deciding whether you have enough information to make a decision, before spending time on the analysis, is a real-world version of this skill.

learningObjectives: Test each statement alone before combining
Recognise when a statement gives a unique answer
Handle ordering, age and arithmetic setups
Avoid using facts from outside the statements

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A statement is sufficient if it leads to exactly one answer to the question. For a yes/no question the answer must be always yes or always no.

coreDefinitions: Sufficient: the information leads to a single, definite answer.
Insufficient: the information leaves two or more different answers possible.
Together: both statements applied at once.
Yes/no question: sufficient only if the answer is always yes or always no.
Setup: facts given before the statements that apply to both.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Imagine every world that fits the statement. If all those worlds give the same answer to the question, the statement is sufficient.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Take statement I alone and ask whether you can build two worlds that give different answers. Repeat for II. If both fail alone, combine them and ask again.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Alone test
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Find two worlds with different answers

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Yes/no rule
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Need always yes or always no
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: x even in some worlds, odd in others: insufficient

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Equation count
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Need as many independent equations as unknowns

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Ordering
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Chains must connect the two items
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: A > C and C > B give A > B

mainNarrative: Ravi's age is asked. Statement I: Ravi is 5 years older than Meena. Statement II: Meena is 20 years old. Alone, I links two unknowns and II gives Meena's age only. Together, Ravi is 25. Both are needed.

For ordering questions, a chain must connect the two people. "Anil is taller than Chandra" and "Chandra is taller than Bala" together give Anil taller than Bala. Alone, neither connects Anil and Bala.
A statement may be sufficient even if it looks indirect. "Three pens cost ₹30" gives the price of one pen at once. "A pen costs less than ₹20" leaves 19 possible prices.
Yes/no questions need a consistent answer. "Is x + y even?" with "Both x and y are odd" is always yes, so it is sufficient. "x is greater than y" leaves both yes and no possible.
When both statements together still leave several answers, the answer is "not sufficient even together". For Priya's age, "older than 18" and "younger than 25" leave 19 to 24.

deepDiveAspects.title: Unique answer vs possible answer
deepDiveAspects.content: A statement can make an answer possible without making it certain; only certainty counts.

deepDiveAspects.title: Redundant statements
deepDiveAspects.content: If a statement repeats the other, together adds nothing.

solvedExamples.title: Both needed
solvedExamples.question: What is Ravi's age? I. Ravi is 5 years older than Meena. II. Meena is 20 years old. Which is correct?

steps.title: Alone
steps.explanation: I links Ravi to Meena; II gives Meena only.

solvedExamples.title: One statement
solvedExamples.question: What is the cost of a pen? I. Three pens cost ₹30. II. A pen costs less than ₹20. Which is correct?

steps.title: II
steps.explanation: Any price below ₹20 fits: not unique.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not

solvedExamples.title: Not even together
solvedExamples.question: What is Priya's age? I. Priya is older than 18. II. Priya is younger than 25. Which is correct?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Even both statements together are not sufficient

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: For each statement try to build two worlds that give different answers. If you can, it is insufficient.

commonMistakes.mistake: Accepting a possible answer as sufficient

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: If the statements repeat each other, together adds nothing.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The answer set is decided by logic, not by calculation of the exact value.

easy.question:
Ravi and Meena are both at most 60 years old, and their ages are whole numbers of years.

Question: What is Ravi's age?
I. Ravi is 5 years older than Meena.
II. Meena is 20 years old.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
easy.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
easy.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 6 and 7). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 1 and 2). Taken together they fix the answer as 25. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

easy.question:
A pen costs a whole number of rupees, at most ₹40.

Question: What is the cost of one pen?
I. Three pens cost ₹30.
II. A pen costs less than ₹20.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
easy.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
easy.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as 10. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 1 and 2). Taken together they fix the answer as 10. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

easy.question:
A basket holds at most 50 apples.

Question: How many apples are in the basket?
I. There are more than 5 apples.
II. The number of apples is a prime number between 20 and 24.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
easy.correctAnswer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
easy.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 6 and 7). Statement II alone fixes the answer as 23. Taken together they fix the answer as 23. Answer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not.

intermediate.question:
x and y are whole numbers from 1 to 9.

Question: Is x + y even?
I. Both x and y are odd.
II. x is greater than y.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
intermediate.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as Yes. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

intermediate.question:
a and b are whole numbers from 1 to 9.

Question: What is the product of a and b?
I. a is twice b, and a + b = 12.
II. a − b = 2.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
intermediate.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as 32. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 3 and 8). Taken together they cannot hold together. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

intermediate.question:
A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹100, ₹200, ₹300, ₹400 or ₹500 and sold it at a profit of 10%, 20%, 25% or 50%.

Question: What was the profit percentage?
I. The cost price was ₹200.
II. The selling price was 25% more than the cost price.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
intermediate.correctAnswer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 10 and 20). Statement II alone fixes the answer as 25. Taken together they fix the answer as 25. Answer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not.

advanced.question:
Five friends Asha, Bilal, Charu, Dev and Esha have five different ages.

Question: Who is the oldest?
I. Bilal is older than Asha and Esha, and Dev is older than Charu but younger than Bilal.
II. Asha is older than Esha.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
advanced.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
advanced.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as Bilal. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example Dev and Charu). Taken together they fix the answer as Bilal. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

advanced.question:
Five friends Asha, Bilal, Charu, Dev and Esha scored different marks in a test.

Question: Who scored the highest?
I. Asha scored more than Bilal and Charu.
II. Dev scored less than Esha, and Esha scored less than Asha.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
advanced.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
advanced.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example Esha and Dev). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example Charu and Bilal). Taken together they fix the answer as Asha. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

placementStyle.question:
x and y are whole numbers from −5 to 5.

Question: Is x greater than y?
I. x² is greater than y².
II. x is positive.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example Yes and No). Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

placementStyle.question:
A two-digit number has a tens digit from 1 to 9 and a units digit from 0 to 9.

Question: What is the number?
I. The sum of its digits is 9.
II. The number is divisible by 5.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Even both statements together are not sufficient
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 18 and 27). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 10 and 15). Taken together they still leave several answers possible (for example 45 and 90). Answer: Even both statements together are not sufficient.

placementStyle.question:
A class has at most 60 boys and at most 60 girls.

Question: How many boys are in the class?
I. The number of boys is 1.5 times the number of girls.
II. The class has 40 students in all.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 3 and 6). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 1 and 2). Taken together they fix the answer as 24. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.
